newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen rising further on IMF news.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen rising further on IMF news.

text.p: Thai stocks were expected to continue advancing on Tuesday on news that Thailand was to seek IMF advice and was studying if an IMF credit line was necessary in order to revive the country's ailing economy, brokers said.
They said reports that Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond had resigned from his post would only have a slight impact on the market because most investors had anticipated the resignation.
The composite SET index closed 34.09 points higher at 680.67 on 8.4 billion baht turnover on Monday. The SET-50 index gained 3.21 points to 52.01.
Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said on Monday that he was meeting five officials of IMF this week in Bangkok to seek their advice on ways to revive the country's battered economy.
Thanong told reporters on Tuesday that he had accepted the central bank governor's resignation and his replacement would be discussed during a cabinet meeting later in the day.

"Those in the financial business have expected Rerngchai would either be forced to resign or would step down from his post because he couldn't serve the government's policy," said Thanadech Mahapokai of Book Club Finance.
